notes:
T424 — the claim/close lifecycle flakes: five defects, one symptom (the kanban disagrees with reality), all five fixed with test-first controls (tools/regression-claim-lifecycle.sh, 19 controls, shown RED on the pre-fix binaries then GREEN, wired into zig build test via build.zig). No engine, artifact, or axiom edits; bars respected.

(1) WORKED-WITHOUT-CLAIMING — the load-bearing one. T392/T395/T400/T404/T419 were worked and committed while the row still read dispatchable; an unclaimed row is invisible to holdsConflict, so holds= and the parallel sets protected nothing. Fix at the natural chokepoint: tools/git-commit-mine now REFUSES a commit whose named task (--task or MANAGENT_TASK_ID) is not in_progress — REFUSE, not warn, decided deliberately: a warn lets the same five rows through and the kanban keeps disagreeing with reality (the brief's own symptom); the recovery is mechanical (managent claim <id> then retry — one command, succeeds whenever the set is free); the wedge case (claim refused: set locked or needs unmet) is a genuine parallel-set/gating violation that SHOULD surface to the human, not a benign friction; and refusal is this repo's established philosophy (T390 done-refusal, T278 scope-refusal, the T282 pre-commit backstop — mechanical refusal, not behavioural warning). The refusal runs BEFORE anything is staged, so the index is left untouched (asserted in the control). --explicit is the deliberate escape, same semantics as the scope escape: the caller takes responsibility and the silent path dies. Statuses done/failed refuse with the amend pointer (the post-close path); blocked refuses naming the unmet gate. A store entry with no status key (synthetic fixtures, T282 arm 8) defaults to allow so the existing regression suite stays green.

(2) POST-CLOSE CORRECTIONS — reopen refused done rows with a dead-end message; T422 hit it when directive D064 landed post-close and the fix had to land in follow-up commit 4330ef2 outside the row. Checked sufficiency first: amend (T317) already recorded corrections and T422's own store record proved it works — the gap was discoverability, not mechanism. Closed it: (a) amend now has an explicit --post-close <text> flavor that records '<ts>: post-close: <text>' WITHOUT touching the verdict (the T422 correction read 'verdict=pass' although the verdict never changed — a post-close record that reads like a verdict change is the same truth problem in miniature; empty or >4KiB text rejected; --post-close and --verdict/--note are mutually exclusive); (b) reopen's done-row refusal now names amend (both flavors) instead of dead-ending; (c) audit now WARNs amended rows (the 'audit flags amended rows' claim in cmdAmend's message was false — audit had no such check; now it does: 'amended post-close (N correction record(s)) — see managent show <id>', WARN level so it surfaces without failing the run). Live effect: the T422 amendment is now surfaced by audit.

(3) add --note was documented in help but ignored by the implementation (note stored null) — the week's signature defect in miniature (T409 found it). cmdAdd now captures --note, validates the same <=4KiB limit dispatch enforces, and stores it on the row; show displays it; the store round-trips. Usage line updated.

(4) CLAIM-AT-CLOSE — measurement first, per the brief. Rows closed after the T390 gate landed (gate commit 2e195f3, 2026-08-06T02:54:47Z): 34. Of those, 3 closed INSIDE the 10s refusal window: T400 (claim->done gap 0s, done 22:30:18Z 08-06), T399 (5s, 23:31:11Z), T404 (4s, 00:26:53Z 08-07) — 3/34 = 8.8%. The number that used --force is UNMEASURABLE from the store: the escape leaves no trace (T400/T404 are also two of the brief's worked-without-claiming rows — claim-at-close is the mechanism by which an unclaimed row closes looking claimed). Verdict: the guard is not effective as prevention (all 3 closed anyway) and its escape is silent — a change IS justified. Minimal fix: a forced within-window close now appends a FORCED amendment ('<done-ts>: FORCED close (claimed Ns before done) — claim-at-close acknowledged via --force'), so the kanban records what the console did instead of looking like a normal close; show and the audit WARN surface it exactly like a manual amend. The window itself stays 10s — no evidence for widening it (T396/T408 at 12s and T405 at 13s sit just outside, but the silent escape, not the window width, is the defect). Caveat on the measurement: a pre-gate binary on those consoles would also explain the within-window closes (the gate binary was deployed with T390's close; --force use is indistinguishable from a stale binary in the store — which is itself the finding that the store cannot tell the truth about claim-at-close).

(5) C10 VOLATILE OVER-COUNT — paths inside fenced code blocks are build-command illustrations (zig --cache-dir, -femit-bin), not evidence citations (Orchestrator ruling on T422, D064). volatileScan now skips CommonMark fenced blocks (3+ backticks or tildes after up to 3 spaces of indent; an opening fence inside a block of the other char is code, not a toggle; an unterminated fence runs to EOF per CommonMark). The fence-marker lines themselves are skipped. Inline code spans (single backticks, the volatile regression's own fixture) are still counted. Census before/after (deployed claimlint, same tree): BEFORE 1065 (213 /tmp, 3 /private/tmp, 25 absolute-outside-tree, 824 untracked/) -> AFTER 879 (125 /tmp, 3 /private/tmp, 23 absolute, 728 untracked/) — delta -186: -88 /tmp, -96 untracked, -2 absolute, /private/tmp unchanged (no such paths inside fences). Sampled dropped tokens are reproduction commands (bin/weizigo-chainability untracked/..., shasum -a 256 untracked/..., --cache-dir /tmp/...) — the class the ruling named. No claimlint floor raised: C10 is report-only and not in claimlint-floor.json; all gated counters byte-identical to the committed baseline (C1a 0, C1b 0, C2 11, C3 48, C6 0, C7 0, C9 0, calibration PASS; C4 45/2, C8 0 unchanged).

Controls (tools/regression-claim-lifecycle.sh, wired into zig build test): 0 null control (claim->work->close cycle succeeds, no added friction); 1 seeded (commit under a dispatchable row REFUSED naming the claim requirement, index untouched; same commit succeeds once claimed; done-row commit refused naming amend; --explicit still commits); 2 seeded (amend --post-close round-trips into store + show; reopen refuses a done row and names amend; audit surfaces the amended row); 3 seeded (add --note round-trips into store + show; >4KiB rejected); 4 seeded (unforced within-window close refused — T390 gate regression; --force close records the FORCED amendment); 5 seeded (a /tmp path inside a fenced block NOT counted by C10 while the same path in prose IS; fixture removed -> paths absent). All managent arms run against a scratch store in /tmp/weizigo (never the live kanban); the claimlint arm uses a fixture doc created and removed in place; the script SKIPs loudly when zig-out binaries are missing (same convention as the T421 volatile and T286 resume regressions). All 19 controls shown RED on the pre-fix binaries (each defect reproduced live: dispatchable-row commit passed silently, amend --post-close died with '--verdict is required', note stored null, oversized note accepted, forced close left no record, fenced path counted) then GREEN after the fixes. Neighbouring regressions re-run clean: git-commit-mine (all arms incl. T282 fixtures with no status key), git-commit-mine-hook, claimlint-volatile (null-control byte-identical), claimlint-output, claimlint-promotion, managent-lock, managent-done-two-phase, duplicate-dispatch, managent-integrity (all 16 — its only failure was the T268 stale-deploy precondition, resolved by the deploy below).

Deployment: zig build deploy (window open; T423 closed 10:38:59Z) + tools/smoke.sh PASS zero STALE (every bin/ tool current at b78648f); bin/managent now carries the new amend/reopen/audit/done behavior; deployed claimlint reports the post-fix census 879. Findings file conforms to the schema (claimlint C7 non-conforming 0). Live kanban touched only by the claim itself; the T423 close and STATE.md M3->L3 relabel in the tree are another console's work, not this row's.

Landmark: advances L1 (the dashboard tells the truth) and L4 (the ledger is clean) — the five ways a row could look finished while the kanban disagreed with reality are now each refused or recorded: unclaimed work is refused at the commit site, post-close corrections land on the row via amend --post-close and are surfaced by audit, add --note round-trips, forced claim-at-close closes leave a FORCED record, and C10 no longer counts reproduction commands as evidence citations.
